pages.text: A neutron-star merger heard by the Laser Interferometer can be found in the sky: point the telescope with its record and photograph the $(thing)kilonova$() - the glow of freshly made gold and platinum, peaking after days: $(item)Kilonova Ash$().

The same mergers, and the collapse of the heaviest stars, launch jets at Γ ≈ 300, beamed into a cone of 1/Γ: $(thing)gamma-ray bursts$(). The $(item)Burst Observatory$() watches the whole sky with twelve scintillators. A low threshold sees more bursts but more noise. Watch until you are 90% sure of a catch, with few false triggers: a $(item)Burst Afterglow Crystal$().
